evals.prompt: I run a small church, ELICM, and our 16th anniversary celebration is Oct 18 with a free dinner and guest speaker. Registration page is https://elicm-anniversary.example.com. We want Facebook ads to get people in our city (mostly families and older adults within 15 miles) to register. Budget is about $15/day for 3 weeks. Give me everything I need to run the ads.
evals.expected_output: A complete copy-paste ad pack: 3+ angles of single-image ads with primary text/headline/description/CTA and creative briefs, a carousel, at least one short video script with shot list, campaign structure with budget, launch checklist, and a review from the expert panel. Should be respectful of religion-related targeting/policy limits.
expectations: Contains at least 3 distinct single-image ads each with primary text, headline, description, and CTA button
Contains a carousel with every card's image concept and headline written out
Contains at least 2 video scripts laid out as shot tables with timing, visual, spoken line, and on-screen text
Each ad names its own aspect ratio/size and an exact on-image text string in its creative brief (not one shared global spec line)
Includes campaign structure: objective, audience/location settings, budget, and a dated schedule
Names a numeric target for the success metric (e.g. cost per lead/registration/purchase) plus explicit kill and scale rules
Hook families are labeled per ad and at least 3 differ; primary-text openers share no sentence
Includes a landing page message-match (ad scent) instruction
No text field, including video spoken lines and on-image text, uses second-person diagnosis of a personal attribute (health condition, religion, age, body, financial status)
Includes a review/critique pass showing concrete changes made (expert panel or equivalent)
Placeholders are limited to facts absent from the prompt, use one consistent token style, and are listed once in a find-and-replace table; no [insert]/TBD/[confirm]
No invented proof statistic (review count, completion rate, customer count) appears in ad copy unless it is a token or came from the prompt
Any weekday written next to a date is correct for that date
Scarcity/urgency claims are tied to a stated real constraint from the prompt or an explicit assumption
Copy states the event is free and names Oct 18 in the headline or first 125 chars of at least one ad
Campaign plan phases the 3 weeks (announce / remind / last call) rather than flat spend
Targeting recommendation uses geography rather than religion as a targeting attribute
Includes first-time setup steps (Pixel/Conversions API or Instant Form fallback, conversion event)
